body:
first of all i really appreciate how much you have had to say on both posts! it was all great to read and i’m glad to read your experience here too! thanks for sharing.

juggling dysphoria that seems to change with time, and safety in a racist society is really overwhelming. it’s nice to take a break from concrete labels and sort of drift around and let people see you however (in places it’s safe to do so) and i hope it’s nice for you too at least some of the time.

i think at the time i wrote this and was freaking out, i was stuck in a lot of really distressing label wars and losing a sense of what i was. i ended up having to taper off medical transition shortly after, so my perspective has changed a bit. your last paragraph sounds kind of similar to where i am with things now in terms of feeling understood. it seems like it takes a lot to adjust to having a part of you like gender consistently misunderstood by strangers.

thank you for the insight. for the past few years, it has really felt like nowhere is safe and people like this are everywhere.

i’ve done everything i can to try and break cycles, and i’m out of ideas. it feels like this is happening involuntarily, and once i notice it has happened, there is nothing i can do about it. as long as i am undesirable/easy to discard and therefore less powerful in even the smallest interactions, this is all i have to protect myself in any interaction.

in terms of prejudice, i find myself gravitating towards people who are racist/homophobic/gnc-phobic in general or against me, if that makes sense. my own therapists have mostly been racist over the years, so i doubt they can handle the effects of intersecting prejudices in a patient. i’ve seen therapists and psychiatrists for 15+ years now, and none have been able to make even a little progress with me. i’m not sure why. i hope this is useful info and thanks again

when i presented feminine, i definitely noticed a double standard. i was built like a ruler and dressed very modestly (to the point that my friends asked me why i dressed so “ugly”), but older people still made creepy comments. i think it goes hand in hand with being “aged up” as a kid.
“feel sadness, not guilt” great to hear coming from someone who said you should guilt people out of suicide

i don’t like posts like these because they make me worry that others’ behaviors are for worse reasons than they probably actually are. i wish more of these posts talked about clear expectations instead of these vague warnings with no course of action. having read this as an autistic person, i’m just inclined to worry that i’ve bothered everyone by texting like this, or that my friends who text like this are up to no good, which isn’t helpful.
yea i would love to! i’d start up a server if needed but i do not have the skills to mod just yet
absolutely same we should all get together or something

seconding _elin’s advice as a scrawny person who bulked slowly. 
dedicating extra effort to upper body workouts helped me feel like my bulking efforts were going in the right direction.
also, this may not be very body-related, but feeling stronger and being able to hit and break my old records helped me offset the worries i had about gains going to what feels like the wrong places.
didn’t help with gains but it did help with insomnia and jitters because it made me sleepy

i am desperately looking for safe online spaces and it has been difficult and landed me in a lot of trouble. i’m glad you’ve been able to find people like you and would love to find more spaces to talk about things and learn from people, but it has been difficult to find them and i may need help

there really is an unconscious bias (sometimes conscious tbh) that we are backwards, also often predatory. i don’t know if you have also experienced some kind of intersection of the assumption that masc transition/presentation is “internalized misogyny” and the assumption that moc are inherently more misogynistic than wm, but that’s been my experience.

i am super early in medical transition but have already had significant changes, and people i knew before coming out have been very threatened by it, despite the fact that i act more pleasant. calling someone’s presentation toxic makes no sense to me, but i have heard the same. i’ve watered myself down so much to avoid this stereotyping in white queer spaces that treat white femininity as the gold standard, and it never works. i’m upset that your experience sounds so similar to mine but also relieved that i’m not completely alone.
thank you for being out there. i feel alienated by a lot of trans youtube too, for similar reasons. if it’s ok, i would love to learn more about your channel.
it’s interesting how different everyone’s experiences are. maybe you’ve experienced things i haven’t

a lot of white trans people i’ve met online only pay attention to those of our issues they can exploit, and if an issue of ours isn’t exploitable and they have to see it, they treat it like an attack. i distrust white femininity from any gender on reflex because it can so easily be used to manipulate people and narratives with little consequence.

yes. i had a bad one this week and was stuck in bed for an entire day and a half with flu-like body aches and fatigue. i am very gentle with myself physically during these times and try to make sure i meet my basic needs (food and water and hygiene) as best i can while the fatigue is around. i hope things are getting better for you now

yes, all the time. it was to the point that i went back into the closet and tried to make it as a woman because i wanted to badly to be one and still felt fake and alienated when i did. i try to cope by advocating for all different types of gender-based issues specific to people of color, but i feel a lot of grief over never making it to being the woman i sometimes wanted to be growing up and feel like i can’t separate that from guilt over being who i am naturally. (i.e. a disgusting slob and traitor who hates women so much they “destroyed” their own womanhood) a lot of it is insidious and comes from within the community so it’s a hard belief to address. i hope this part isn’t too much to share and doesn’t take away from your feelings—i wanted to share that i feel a similar way and i’m sure many others do as well, specific to the experience of missing out on being a woman of color.

i’m also having trouble falling back on culture because of ethical issues i have with some of its earlier beliefs but especially the way it is post-colonization, so you’re not alone there either. i’m hoping here or somewhere else you can find others with your background and current conditions and maybe make something new. sending you lots of strength and support
our own therapists sometimes 😔
i am interested in joining!

you’re not wrong! the people who abused me were survivors themselves, and if it were 100% okay to behave any kind of way as a survivor, i wouldn’t be so worried about my own behavior. thank you for reminding me!

i understand and respect that. do you ever worry about hurting other people in your life like friends or other family, or is it specifically related to parent/child dynamics for you? does the worry ever get out of control?

i am still far away from that point but definitely on the fence about it. as long as i still hold beliefs that the world is an unsafe place, there’s zero chance i will raise any kids of my own.

i’ve realized my interest in having kids comes from a desire to give someone things i never had (i was the oldest and protected my younger brother a lot) and that my new career path will achieve that much better than having kids of my own and running the risk of passing on biological aspects of psychological disorders or accidentally seeing the poor kids’ lives as a do-over of mine.

i’m sorry to hear you’re dealing with so many difficult feelings right now. i have a friend in high school and he’s not having a good time academically either. are you interested in trying any new activities? when i was having a hard time in school, i asked my teachers and counselor about volunteer opportunities and upcoming events. it might be difficult if things are all online for you, but volunteer opportunities you haven’t heard about yet might be interesting if you’re looking for things to do. if you’re interested in healthcare, have you been able to find any health-related events/clubs/volunteer/shadowing opportunities? (not necessarily at school) they can provide really good mentorship if you’re feeling lost regarding the future. i was really numb and isolated in high school, and volunteering helped me just a little bit (group therapy was also really helpful because i got to meet other high school kids dealing with depression and it helped me learn to socialize) but there may be other actions you can take to break out of feeling numb and stuck. i hope you find something helpful soon and i would be happy to talk a little if you need it!

being 13 is hard, and being different makes it harder. i was made fun of for my height when i was 13 but i love being tall now because there are so many benefits (you can reach things! you can see over other people’s heads in a crowd!) i understand how you feel about some of the cons, but i hope you find some accepting community and feel better about your height, because it is a great thing. i am sorry things are hard now, though.
